query: To reveal how feeding encoding is organized in the continuous UMAP space, the UMAP embedding of all neurons from 14 animals is colored by whether each neuron is feeding-activated or feeding-inhibited (based on the sign of the CePNEM-derived feeding tuning), showing that feeding encoding is graded along one axis of the UMAP space.

analyse_plan.Objective: Show that velocity encoding features are systematically organized along a continuous gradient in the UMAP encoding space.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Same UMAP coordinates as Fig_3A; color gradient should be smooth, not patchy.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the CePNEM posterior particles for every behavior-encoding neuron in the 14 SWF415 animals, the per-neuron CePNEM-derived feeding-tuning slope (feedingness) values, and the per-neuron significance flags for feeding encoding from the deconvolved-activity-matrix tests (x1 = 0.125/signal, x2 = 0.25 · sD/sM, Bonferroni + Benjamini-Hochberg, FDR = 0.05). 2. Build UMAP Reference Space: Construct a 19200-dimensional behavioral context vector by concatenating the velocity, head curvature, and feeding traces from 12 SWF415 animals; sample 4004 median CePNEM fits across all 14 animals, evaluate each on this concatenated context to produce a 4004 × 19200 matrix of model-predicted activities, and run UMAP on this matrix to obtain a 2D embedding. 3. Project All Posterior Particles: For every neuron, project each of its posterior particles into the precomputed UMAP space using the same context vectors. 4. Classify Feeding Tuning: For each neuron that significantly encodes feeding, classify it as feeding-activated (positive feedingness slope) or feeding-inhibited (negative feedingness slope) using the Cartesian average m_cart of its hierarchical-model fit. 5. Save Key Results: Save the per-neuron UMAP point clouds, the per-neuron feeding-tuning classifications (feeding-activated vs feeding-inhibited), and the colormap parameters used for the panel. 6. Visualization: Plot every posterior particle from every feeding-encoding neuron as a dot in the UMAP embedding, colored by feeding-tuning class (feeding-activated in green, feeding-inhibited in magenta), with non-feeding-encoding neurons rendered in a low-saturation background tone.

key_analysis_results: Velocity encoding was graded along one UMAP axis, with forward-active neurons on one side and reverse-active on the other. The gradient was smooth and continuous, with no discrete boundary between forward and reverse encoding.
key_analysis_conclusions: Velocity encoding is organized as a smooth gradient in the neural population, consistent with the continuous encoding landscape identified in Fig_3A.

summary_report.abstract: UMAP colored by forwardness reveals velocity encoding organized as a smooth gradient.
summary_report.methods: Same UMAP as Fig_3A, colored by CePNEM-derived forwardness (velocity slope).
summary_report.results: Velocity graded along one axis: forward-active on one side, reverse-active on the other. Smooth gradient.
summary_report.discussion: Demonstrates that velocity encoding varies continuously across the population rather than forming discrete forward/reverse clusters.
